title: Who else does this?
author: verbalbacklash
selftext:
I was lying in bed Sunday night, trying to go to sleep while thinking about the game I've been working on. The thought hit me that one piece of it could easily be turned into a casual mini-game I'd actually enjoy playing on its own. It would also solve a personal problem needing a clean, ad-free game for travel or downtime you know, when you’re sitting at the airport waiting for a flight or stuck in a dentist’s waiting room with just enough time to either doom scroll or play something silly.

I don't know about you, but the number of hours I’ve poured into games like Bejeweled, Minesweeper, and classic tower defense is maddening when I think about it. So I thought, why not just make my own little time-wasters?

I knocked one out in two days with all the features I wanted, shared it with few friends across a few formats, and posted it in a couple of places. Now I’m sitting here thinking about how great it is that AI lets you build what you want to play so fast that it never feels like a chore. Plus, it’s a custom game with no ads and no microtransactions just your monthly AI subscription of choice.

Thoughts? Does anyone else build little casual games just for the fun of playing something you thought up the night before, with zero intention to monetize?

Side note: Honestly, it feels like most of the games I've been working on are free "for fun" projects anyway, because A) that's really what they are, and B) I'm definitely not a professional game dev!

comments.author: KeismeyStudio
comments.body: On a exactement le même état d'esprit !

comments.author: olafthemanofsnow
comments.body:
I agree with the sentiment but as a father of two, I would take it one step further.

My eldest daughter is 7 and she has recently got into gaming (much to mums disappointment), but I have watched her go from failing badly at astro bot to now finishing spiderman 2.

And she always comes to me with ideas of games she wants to play. And we have started building and designing them together. Our first joint project is a simple game where you care for and look after a dog. She tells me what she wants to be able to do, such as take it for a walk, feed it, bath it etc and we go away and think about how to make it fun. 

I also added a layer of education to it so that she knows why she should do those things (but she hasnt noticed its teaching her).

We are actually hoping to release it as a small mobile game in the future. But the building and bonding has been the biggest reward.

replies.body: this man this, probably one of the most positive post I have ever read about using AI. Not only teaching but bonding that's huge. This has just brightened my day thank you.
